assessment: This paper presents a detailed single-molecule, multi-color microscopy study of the real-time assembly of perfringolysin O, a member of the membrane attack complex perforin cholesterol-dependent cytolysin superfamily. With the ability to resolve different reaction species simultaneously with membrane leakage, this work provides key mechanistic details including identifying assemblies involved in membrane lysis, and how membrane binding, oligomerization, and pore transitioning depends on concentration and pH. This study will be of interest to many, particularly those studying cytolysin mechanisms, but also the broader field of single-molecule studies of membrane binding proteins.
